content: [Discord DM charlie_partner Sat Apr 05 15:00 UTC 2026] Hi, I'm trying to understand NebulaTech's SLA credit policy. For Atlassian Enterprise, if the uptime is 99.92% in a given month, what credit percentage applies? I've heard it might be 10% from the standard tier.

For Atlassian Enterprise at 99.92% uptime: the applicable tier is the Enterprise-exclusive 99.90%–99.95% tier, which provides a **5% credit** (not 10%). The 10% tier applies to uptime below 99.90%. Source: https://www.atlassian.com/legal/sla

[Discord DM charlie_partner Sat Apr 05 15:10 UTC 2026] Interesting — so the 5% tier is specific to Enterprise, not Premium? And what about AWS EC2 — if our EC2 uptime is 98.5%, what credit percentage would that get?

Correct: the 5% credit tier (99.90%–99.95%) is Enterprise-exclusive. Premium plan starts credit at < 99.90% (10% tier).

For AWS EC2 at 98.5% uptime: this falls in the 95.0%–99.0% range, which qualifies for a **30% service credit** (source: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/sla/). This is higher than the 10% tier (99.0%–99.99%) and lower than the 100% tier (< 95.0%).
[Discord DM charlie_partner Sat Apr 05 15:20 UTC 2026] Got it. One more: when is the AWS EC2 credit claim deadline?

AWS EC2 credit claim deadline: end of the **second billing cycle** following the incident month (source: https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/sla/). For an incident in 2024-11, the second billing cycle ends 2025-01-31.
